prompt: The page title is wrapped in an h1 tag so the browser knows it's the main heading.
why: Tags describe what each part is. Choosing h1 for the main heading is HTML structure.
trap: It helps accessibility too, but the clue is picking the right tag.

prompt: A 'button' made from a plain div can't be reached with the Tab key; switching to a real button tag fixes it.
tells: switching to a real button tag fixes it
why: Using the element that matches the job gives built-in behaviour. That's HTML structure.
trap: Keyboard access improves, but the fix is the right tag.

prompt: The steps are written as a ul with li items instead of lines separated by line breaks.
why: Lists have their own tags. Marking up content as what it is, is HTML structure.
trap: Layout comes from CSS; here it's the meaning of the content.

prompt: To go to another page, the text is wrapped in an a tag with an href.
tells: wrapped in an a tag with an href
why: Links are a basic HTML element. No JavaScript needed.
trap: A click happens, but the link works from the tag alone.

prompt: A closing tag in the wrong place made the footer end up inside the article.
tells: A closing tag in the wrong place
why: Tags nest inside each other, and a misplaced closing tag changes the structure.
trap: The DOM reflects it, but the mistake is in the HTML.

prompt: The page uses header, nav, main and footer instead of a dozen plain divs.
why: Meaningful tags describe the page's parts. That's HTML structure.
trap: It helps screen readers, but the clue is the tags themselves.
